The gold's javadoc promises a copy of the fields of the JSON Object starting with the field name the parser points to; a buffer in which every field name appears twice is not that copy. No one-line edit above the gold restores it: the gold copies the current event and then the structure at the same token for every field, whatever token a caller starts it at. The convention (a field written as its name once, then the value copied from the value token) is pinned outside the gold: TokenBuffer.copyCurrentStructure (for a FIELD_NAME: writeFieldName, nextToken, then the value), BeanDeserializer.deserializeWithUnwrapped and BuilderBasedDeserializer.deserializeWithUnwrapped (p.nextToken() to the value, then writeFieldName(propName) and copyCurrentStructure(p)), with TestJacksonTypes testTokenBufferWithSample, TestTokenBuffer testWithJSONSampleDoc and TestUnwrapped testSimpleUnwrappedDeserialize passing.
